lines.text: Ecological services are the various kinds of beneﬁts humans receive from the natu-

ecosystems worldwide are under enormous pressure from human activities, especially
from many land use projects. Therefore, it is important to remind people that the
loss of these services will leave us worse oﬀ.(IUCN, 2005)

5. Metrics for assessing ecological services value (coeﬃcient
set α)
To approximate the coeﬃcients given due to various ecological services, we ﬁrst
deﬁne the term ”ecological services” in more accurate categories.
The categories
below are similar to The Millennium Ecosystem Assessment (MA), a major UN-
sponsored eﬀort to analyze the impact of human actions on ecosystems and human
well-being.(Board, 2005)
• Provisioning Services

spans.text: A provisioning service is any type of beneﬁt to people that can be extracted from

lines.text: A provisioning service is any type of beneﬁt to people that can be extracted from
nature. Along with food, other types of provisioning services include drinking

spans.text: water, timber, wood fuel, natural gas, oils, plants that can be made into clothes

lines.text: water, timber, wood fuel, natural gas, oils, plants that can be made into clothes
and other materials, and medicinal beneﬁts.
• Regulating Services

spans.text: A regulating service is the beneﬁt provided by ecosystem processes that moder-

lines.text: A regulating service is the beneﬁt provided by ecosystem processes that moder-
ate natural phenomena. Regulating services include pollination, decomposition,
water puriﬁcation, erosion and ﬂood control, and carbon storage and climate
regulation.
• Cultural Services

spans.text: A cultural service is a non-material beneﬁt that contributes to the development

lines.text: A cultural service is a non-material beneﬁt that contributes to the development
and cultural advancement of people, e.g. the building of knowledge and the

spans.text: spreading of ideas; creativity born from interactions with nature; and recreation.

lines.text: spreading of ideas; creativity born from interactions with nature; and recreation.
• Supporting Services
The most fundamental natural processes that allow the Earth to sustain basic
life forms, such as photosynthesis, nutrient cycling, the creation of soils, and
the water cycle. These processes are the basis for provisional, regulating, and
cultural services.

7.2 case 2: China Baowu Steel Group
Steel, as a necessary material in many diﬀerent area from military use to
the structure of buildings, has played an important role since the Worlds
Industrial Revolution. Steel industry thus has been seen as the key to
economic prosperity. Large steel companies could generate employment,
export earnings and tax revenues. However other than these social bene-
ﬁts, steel industry also has a signiﬁcant impact to environment.

lines.text: The process of making steel starts from the production of iron. Iron is made from
iron ore going through reduction reaction with carbon monoxide under extreme high
temperature. The carbon monoxide using here is made from heating carbon with
oxygen. The side products of this reaction contribute to major air emission in the
process of making iron which are carbon dioxide, sulﬁde and nitride. Methods for

spans.text: manufacturing steel from iron involve basic oxygen steelmaking(BOS) and electric arc

Thus, due to the huge production of steel and various side product involved and

ignored.

8. Discussion and Conclusion
From the analysis and results from the case studies, we can conclude that this
model can eﬀectively estimate the value of ecological services from diﬀerent types
of land use projects. By analysing the coeﬃcients set and applying this model to
various land use projects, the process of understanding the true economic costs of
these projects will be more accurate with detailed and appropriate considerations of
ecosystem services.
This model provides a way to easily view the threshold of value creation and
maximization. Despite the strength of the model shown in the case studies, it also
reveals its limitations. To accurately represent the value of the project in speciﬁc
cases, the coeﬃcients in the model has to be chosen carefully to best illustrate the
type and impact brought by the project. Also, this model relies on the assumption
that the value and cost generated across the area is uniform, which is not necessarily
true in reality. To improve this model, we suggest dividing the area into various
sections by various land types and use diﬀerent coeﬃcients. Thus this model could
become a summation of many small sections.
